migration_surface_label: Example State official voter-information host-transition policy
delivery_role_note: Domain moves, .gov adoption, emergency replacement hosts, and legacy-host recovery shape whether voters can still recognize and reach the current official voter-information source during a hostname transition.
url_mapping_policy_note: Old URLs either map one-to-one to the new host, route to an explicit superseding page, or route to the ordinary office/help lane when there is no safe one-to-one successor.
redirect_policy_note: Server-side permanent redirects are preferred once the move is live; generic homepage collapse is avoided when it would destroy scope or election-cycle context.
old_domain_retention_note: The prior host remains under trusted control and keeps TLS current while recovery redirects remain active so the old domain does not fall into the wrong hands.
search_move_support_note: Where applicable, old/new site verification, Change of Address signaling, and monitoring were completed as support evidence for the move, but public routing behavior remains the controlling artifact.
sitemap_update_note: The new host publishes the current sitemap set and the migration review records whether search-discovery feeds were updated to the new URLs.
canonical_update_note: Canonical annotations on the new host point to the new URLs rather than preserving the superseded host as the representative URL.
alternate_language_update_note: If translated equivalents exist, alternate-language declarations are updated to the new host so multilingual discovery moves with the migration.
email_transition_note: Legacy email addresses remain aliased or otherwise safely handled during the transition so old contact lanes do not silently break.
partner_channel_update_note: Official partner directories, community relays, and platform listings are reviewed so they do not keep teaching the superseded host as current.
offline_materials_update_note: Printed materials, QR destinations, signage, and other offline branding are reviewed on a migration timeline so old-host carriers still recover safely.
emergency_replacement_policy_note: If a temporary replacement host is used, it is explicitly labeled as temporary current state and linked back to the ordinary office/help lane and later steady-state host.
